note: v1 93.47 (seeds 0/11 93.47/93.43), first draft of PEAK-TIME WAREHOUSE, 'the one comes home' - the answer to Where Is the One. For the intro and the first groove the kick sits on the OFF-beats with the hats and short hoover stabs confirming that wrong grid, so you hear it all shifted by an eighth. In the break the kick leaves and a giant synthesised voice (an octave down, formants pulled lower with wM's new formant-preserving pitch) chants 'one' on the true downbeats over a hoover swell and a snare roll; the drop lands the kick, the claps and the A minor hoover stab on those ones and the grid snaps over. The peak layers the distorted kick, a reese and the voice every four bars; the outro lets the kick slip back to the off-beats. Rumble bass from the kick's dark hall. 140 bpm, 4:09.

v2 93.46 (seeds 0/11 93.46/93.43, level with v1 93.47/93.43): THE HELD BREATH, a polish of the reveal rather than a new layer. The beat before the drop is now silence: the giant voice's last 'one', the snare roll at sixteenths, then nothing for one beat, and then the kick lands on the true one and the grid snaps home - the homecoming hits out of a gap instead of out of the roll. (Tried with the intro's kick also held back eight bars, as in Where Is the One: it broke the join from The Gallop Splits, flow 36 -> 9, and delayed the displaced-grid setup this track depends on, so the kick still starts at once here.)

v3 93.56 (seeds 0/11 93.56/93.54 vs v2 re-scored 93.73/93.70): a peak that unfolds instead of arriving all at once - taking away, after Harry's 'too busy... all comes in too fast' note on another track. The peak used to drop the distorted kick, the ride, the voice, the reese, the home stab AND its answer all on bar one; now the home stab and its answer a minor third up alternate bar by bar instead of stacking, and the reese waits sixteen bars, so the peak opens on the hard kick, the ride and the giant voice and the bass rolls in halfway - a second lift inside the peak. Slightly lower by the metric (-0.17), kept because it breathes.

v4 94.03 (seeds 0/11 94.03/94.02 vs v3 re-scored 93.11/93.11): A CLEANER FLOOR - a mix polish of the low end, Harry's 'kick/bass weight, clarity'. The low end sat 7-8 dB over the genre at 44, 62 and 160-210 Hz: the 909's punch and the rumble's reverb tail were smearing into one boom. The rumble send is down 2 dB and the master gets three narrow cuts (44 Hz -3, 62 Hz -3, 180 Hz -5), so each kick lands as a punch with the rumble breathing behind it, and the giant voice and the hoover sit clear above. Spectrum 92 -> 98.
